items.title: [persistent] THE STALE-INDEX REVERT HAZARD HAS A ONE-LINE NON-DESTRUCTIVE REPAIR, and the armed set is found by crossing TWO diffs
AJC TEAM THREAD — four lanes, one project, use this instead of re-deriving each others work
CROSS-PROJECT THREAD — AJC and AJCR are doing the same mathematics twice; this is where you stop that
SUBAGENT FINAL REPORTS STALL AT 187 BYTES WHILE THEIR FINDINGS ARRIVE BY INBOX -- sixth occurrence in lane ajc-pic0av, and this time the report-now prompt did not help either.
AJC.picrep is done with three pending children (.quot/.serre/.tensor) — recorded, not fixed; it is no AJCR lane's row
ROOT BUILD IS RED IN YOUR FILE RIGHT NOW -- probably your in-flight edit, flagging in case it is not
A 17k-LINE SORRY-FREE PORT LANDS ON A CARRIER WITH NO SHEAF-SIDE FACE -- front (a) of AJC.pic0av

commits.subject: The commit recording the hazard re-armed it: cross the WHOLE index AFTER every commit, not just your own paths
commits.summary:
**Seventh confirmation, and the sharpest form.** The commit I made to record the sixth immediately re-armed the hazard: it named only `.archon-horizon/inbox` paths, yet the cross afterwards showed two newly armed LEAN paths I never staged -- including 258 lines of another lane new `Albanese/TensorPowerCoproduct.lean`, which my next broad commit would have deleted. Cause: that lane landed the file between two of my reads, so my index held pre-commit blobs. Cleared; disks verified unchanged.

**So the recipe needs strengthening.** "Commit, then `git add -- <same paths>`" is not sufficient, because the arming is produced by a concurrent writer rather than by what you staged. The check is: cross the WHOLE index after EVERY commit, unconditionally, and repeat until it returns empty. Recorded on I-0656.

commits.subject: The armed-index set regenerated 20 minutes after I cleared it, holding 158 lines of another project
commits.summary:
**Sixth I-0656 confirmation, and the operational correction that matters.** Clearing the armed set once per session is not enough: after my earlier clear it regenerated within ~20 minutes, the second time holding four entries of which three were deletions against `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` (1 + 145 + 12 lines) with disk byte-identical to HEAD. Cleared, re-crossed, disks re-verified. Both times every armed path lay in a project this lane never touched.

**A signature distinction for the gitignored exception.** The fourth entry (`scripts/partition-probe.lean`) is 69 INSERTIONS for a file not on disk -- it would add a file rather than revert one, so it is harmless as well as unclearable. The dangerous signature is deletions with disk == HEAD; insertions-only for an absent path is noise.

**And a close-out false alarm worth recording**: the AJC root module mismatched HEAD, which was ajc-albanese uncommitted disk edit, not damage -- all three of this session imports are in HEAD. In a multi-lane run, diff the direction and check whether your own lines survive, rather than whether the file matches.

commits.subject: Close-out: the 187-byte subagent stall is a report-handoff failure, not an idle agent
commits.summary:
**Seventh and eighth occurrence of I-0677, with the datum that narrows it.** Both subagents this session reported 187 bytes while their underlying transcripts grew to 120KB and 189KB and were still growing. So the agents were doing substantial real work and the failure is in the final-report handoff, not in execution -- a distinction earlier notes on that item could not draw. The 187-byte file is a symlink; its stat size is the link, not the target.

**What made the session survivable**: I ran all three of the janitor's assigned checks myself in parallel rather than blocking on it -- commit verification against HEAD, the stale-claim sweep over both retractions, and the collection-health triage. That is what found the live armed revert against an AJCR file this lane never touched.

commits.subject: Close-out state: the stale-index revert was armed against a project this lane never touched
commits.summary:
**Fifth confirmation of I-0656, and a new variant.** The two-diff cross at close-out found the shared index holding a pre-commit blob that would DELETE 20 lines of `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/.../DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean` -- a project this AJC lane never touched and a file it never opened. Disk and HEAD agreed; only the index was stale. Repaired with the one-line `hgit add -- <path>` and re-crossed to empty over the whole ledger. So the armed set is NOT confined to the current lane write set: checking only your own paths passes while leaving a live revert aimed elsewhere.

**A roadmap warning correctly left standing.** `AJC.jacobian.assembly` warns "every sub-item done, consider done" and must stay pending: its detail is "Package the final Jacobian witness", which rests on `AJC.pic0av` -- a SIBLING row, invisible to the child-status arithmetic, and still 0/3 with five live sorries. Arithmetically right, substantively wrong; recorded on I-0638 so the next pass does not reopen it.

commits.subject: Locate what is still owed for dim Pic^0 <= g: the presentation gives n + #sigma, and sharpening to n needs the relations to be regular
commits.summary:
**A checked statement rather than a docstring claim.** `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_ringKrullDim_le` (axiom-clean) records what a standard-smooth presentation gives for free: surjecting from `MvPolynomial ι k` and using `MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_of_isNoetherianRing` bounds $\dim S$ by $\#\iota = n + \#\sigma$. Stated existentially because $\iota,\sigma$ are bound inside the class field, so naming them in the conclusion would require choosing a presentation first.

**The gap, named.** That is the WEAK bound -- it is $n$ only when there are no relations. Sharpening to $\dim S \le n$ needs the $\#\sigma$ relations to cut dimension by exactly $\#\sigma$, i.e. to be a regular sequence. True for a standard-smooth presentation (the Jacobian is invertible) but genuine commutative algebra, and mathlib at this pin has no ringKrullDim-of-a-standard-smooth-algebra lemma. `Albanese/StandardSmoothDimension.lean` proves the matching LOWER bound by the same technique, so it is the model for the missing half rather than a source of it.

**Probe re-run after the additions**: 8 declarations clean, both controls (`topologicalKrullDim_eq_genus_of_forall_finrank_cotangentSpace_le`, `finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne`) correctly report `sorryAx`. My five modules build, 8698 jobs exit 0. The root build currently fails in `Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`, which is ajc-fbc lane with 96 uncommitted lines in flight -- not touched here.

commits.subject: The inequality was not merely in mathlib -- it was already used inline in this project, and named in the prose of the file measured as lacking it
commits.summary: **Sharpening my own correction.** `Albanese/AuslanderBuchsbaum.lean:2239` already applies `ringKrullDim_le_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal` inline, and `Albanese/StandardSmoothDimension.lean:211` -- the file whose absence of an upper bound r5 measured and recorded -- states the fact in prose in its own docstring. What was missing was never the mathematics or even the mathlib lemma, but a named reusable statement at the scheme level. A fact used inside one proof body and mentioned in one docstring is invisible to every search that looks for a declaration.

commits.subject: Front (a)'s wall is not the port: 17k sorry-free lines land on a carrier with no sheaf-side face
commits.summary:
**The decisive grep.** AJCR `Scheme.CechPic` is a self-contained definitional Picard group; its ONLY bridge to invertible sheaves is `cechPicEquivPic`, which carries `[IsAffine X]` irremovably (it needs a trivializing basic open per point plus `Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top` over $\Gamma(X,\top)$). No non-affine comparison exists in either project or in mathlib -- which has no Picard group of a SCHEME at all, only ring-level `CommRing.Pic`.

**Why that is fatal.** Clause (iii) compares a kernel of `PicSharp.relPresheaf` -- a setoid quotient of `LineBundle.OnProduct`, honest invertible sheaves -- against a Cech $\check{H}^1$ on $C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k[\varepsilon]$, a PROPER CURVE. Not affine, and not affine precisely BECAUSE the $\varepsilon$-kernel is nonzero: on an affine with trivial Picard group there is nothing to compute. The one hypothesis the dictionary needs is what the problem structurally denies.

**Priced both ways per I-0678, and both are large -- itself the signal.** Import closure of the three endpoint files: 57 modules, 46 absent from AJC, 13,691 lines. Closure of the 10-file genuine core: 76 modules, 60 absent, 17,031 lines. All sorry-free. The size is not the objection; a multi-session port is plausible. The objection is that you finish holding a class in `X.CechPic` with no theorem connecting it to `LineBundle.OnProduct`.

**So the residue is one missing statement, not four theorems**: Cech $\check{H}^1$ of units on a NON-AFFINE scheme $\cong$ invertible sheaf classes. New mathematics for this workspace. Recorded at the sorry docstring, on the `AJC.pic0av.tangent` row that had recommended the port for three rounds, and as inbox I-0689 with the general rule -- ask what CARRIER a port leaves you holding and whether it has the FACE your consumer needs.

commits.subject: Roadmap: the ambient properness route is dead on all three rows, and the dimension <= half is clean
commits.summary:
**Three rows corrected.** `AJC.pic0av.structure` had recommended the refuted ambient route as "worth trying first"; the parent `AJC.pic0av` called properness "attackable three ways: from the ambient Pic, ..."; `AJC.pic0av.identity` carried the "genuinely absent" verdict on the dimension bound. Each now states what was measured, what was concluded wrongly from it, and which route survives.

**Both corrections are of the same kind**, which is why they are one commit: a conclusion drawn from a correct observation about the wrong object. The properness measurement was right about the closed immersion and wrong about which scheme is quasi-compact; the dimension measurement was right about `StandardSmoothDimension.lean` and wrong about which invariant the chain produces.

commits.subject: Retract the 'genuinely absent' verdict where it lives -- both docstrings asserted it as fact
commits.summary:
**Two surviving sites**, found by grepping the phrase rather than assuming the new file superseded them: `Pic0Dimension.lean:246` stated "the ≤ direction is genuinely absent rather than merely unlocated" as a measured conclusion, and `IdentityComponent.lean` repeated it under `finrank_eq_genus`. What the original measurement correctly established -- that `StandardSmoothDimension.lean` carries no `ringKrullDim` upper bound -- is retained; only the conclusion drawn from it is retracted.

**Both now point forward** to `topologicalKrullDim_le_genus_of_forall_finrank_cotangentSpace_le` (axiom-clean, no `PerfectField`) and say what is genuinely still owed: the uniform COTANGENT bound, which is a statement about embedding dimensions rather than about dimension theory. Kernel-checked, both modules built.

commits.subject: THE 'GENUINELY ABSENT' HALF OF dim Pic^0 = g WAS A MEASUREMENT OF THE WRONG QUANTITY -- and it needs no regularity and no perfect field
commits.summary:
**The inequality.** $\dim R \le \dim_{\kappa}(\mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2)$ for EVERY Noetherian local ring -- Krull height theorem (`ringKrullDim_le_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal`) composed with Nakayama (`IsLocalRing.spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace`), both already in the pinned mathlib. `spanFinrank` occurred in exactly one AJC file, for an unrelated purpose. Regularity is the case of EQUALITY, and that iff was the only form the project had.

**What the previous measurement got wrong.** `Pic0Dimension` recorded the $\le$ direction as "genuinely absent rather than merely unlocated", having searched `Albanese/StandardSmoothDimension.lean` for a `ringKrullDim` UPPER bound and found only lower ones at maximal ideals. It searched for a bound on the wrong invariant: the chapter produces COTANGENT dimensions, and the conversion to Krull dimension is unconditional in exactly this direction.

**AXIOM-CLEAN, measured with two controls that both fire `sorryAx`** (`finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne`, `genus_le_topologicalKrullDim_of_isRegular`): all four new general bricks, and `Pic0.topologicalKrullDim_le_genus_of_forall_finrank_cotangentSpace_le`. The `=` form correctly still leaks through front (a). So the $\le$ direction of Milne III.1 Rmk 1.4(e) is now clean at `Pic^0`, gated on a cotangent bound alone.

**And it drops the `PerfectField` binder.** The existing $=$ theorem carries `[PerfectField k]`, inherited irremovably from `isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_of_perfectField`. Under the owner decision I-0491 the headline is over an ARBITRARY field, so that was a real gap. The new $=$ form takes regularity at the identity as a hypothesis and carries no field condition; the asymmetry is the mathematics -- $\ge$ genuinely needs a regular point, since at a cusp the embedding dimension exceeds the dimension.

commits.subject: Retraction notes on the two ambient-properness nodes, and the flag that swallowed my first attempt
commits.summary:
**Node-scoped failure memory** for `universallyClosed_of_ambient` and `proper_of_ambient_universallyClosed`, per the house rule that Lean progress notes belong on the hgraph node rather than in blueprint prose. Both record that the theorem is true, the hypothesis unsatisfiable, and which lemma to use instead.

**A CLI trap worth the record.** `graph add comment` takes `--content` / `--content-file`, NOT `--body` (which `inbox comment` takes). Called with `--body` it exited 0, echoed my text back through the pager, and wrote NOTHING -- `grep -c` on the node file returned 0. It also rejects a fully-qualified declaration name as `target` and wants the node id. Read back every state-mutating CLI call on disk.

commits.subject: THE AMBIENT PROPERNESS REDUCTION REDUCED NOTHING: UniversallyClosed forces CompactSpace, and Pic is an infinite disjoint union
commits.summary:
**The refutation.** Mathlib derives `QuasiCompact` from `UniversallyClosed` (the `priority := 900` instance -- precisely why `IsProper` has no quasi-compactness field), and `Spec k` is compact, so `UniversallyClosed (PicScheme C).hom` would force `CompactSpace (PicScheme C).left`. But $\mathrm{Pic}_{C/k}=\bigsqcup_{d\in\mathbb{Z}}\mathrm{Pic}^d$ -- the Kleiman th:main(1) clause `HasPicScheme` itself bundles -- and an infinite disjoint cover by nonempty opens has no finite subcover.

**Trap (c), undetectable by every standard check.** `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_ambient` and `proper_of_ambient_universallyClosed` are true, sorry-free and axiom-clean, and they reduce nothing: their hypothesis is unsatisfiable. No sorry census or axiom probe can see this, because a theorem with a false antecedent is still a theorem. Retracted at all four docstring sites; the theorems are retained, since the closed-immersion transport is right for a FINITE ambient union.

**New, sorry-free:** `not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` (pure topology), `Scheme.compactSpace_of_universallyClosed` (the mathlib chain as one name), and `Scheme.not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` / `not_isProper_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`. Stated at scheme generality with no Picard vocabulary; deliberately NOT instantiated at `PicScheme C`, which would need the degree decomposition of the scheme that this project lacks.

**What survives is what the roadmap called the fallback.** `proper_of_valuativeCriterion` quantifies over `(Pic0Scheme C).hom`, whose source IS quasi-compact (`Pic0.quasiCompact`, r0009), so it is untouched -- and it was never a fallback but the only route. Also rooted `Pic0Dimension` and the new file into `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` per I-0600: r5 left its two new files off the root, so the workspace axiom probe covered none of them.
